stem: Five people -- Ajay, Birju, Chhaya, Dhruv, and Esha -- sit in a row of five seats numbered 1 (leftmost) to 5 (rightmost). The following clues apply: (1) Esha sits at the rightmost seat. (2) Birju, Chhaya, and Dhruv occupy three consecutive seats in that left-to-right order. (3) Ajay does not sit in any of the last three seats (seats 3, 4, or 5). Who sits in the fourth seat from the left?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Esha=5, Ajay=1 (only end not taken by Esha and satisfying clue 3), leaving seats 2-3-4 for Birju-Chhaya-Dhruv in order; seat 4 = Dhruv.
Student ignores clue 3, places Birju-Chhaya-Dhruv at seats 1-2-3, and puts Ajay at seat 4.
Student reverses clue 1, treating Esha as the leftmost (seat 1) instead of rightmost; this forces Birju-Chhaya-Dhruv to seats 3-4-5, putting Ajay at seat 2 and Chhaya at seat 4.
Student reads clue 2 right-to-left (turning the stated left-to-right order around), placing Dhruv-Chhaya-Birju at seats 2-3-4, giving seat 4 = Birju.

explanation: Clue 1 fixes Esha at seat 5. Clue 3 limits Ajay to seat 1 or 2; since Esha holds seat 5 and the Birju-Chhaya-Dhruv block (clue 2) needs three consecutive seats, testing the block at seats 1-2-3 forces Ajay to seat 4 or 5 (violates clue 3), so the block sits at seats 2-3-4 with Ajay at seat 1. Seat 4 = Dhruv.
